raw_text:
- The focus is on analyzing completion-time differences among sites using identical nominal work processes.
- The scope includes examining measurable factors and observations to distinguish competing explanations.

Assumptions
- Variations in completion times are due to factors beyond simple process variation.
- Completion times can be reliably measured and analyzed to distinguish cause.

Research design
- Randomized controlled experiment (RCE) to isolate and compare the effects of hypothesized factors.
- Observational study to gather initial insights from existing data.
- Cross-sectional time series to analyze temporal patterns in performance metrics.

Data or evidence needed
- Precise measurements of completion times.
- Documentation of work processes and checkpoints.
- Observations on factors such as employee working hours, work environment, and available resources.
- Historical data on process improvements and any associated changes in performance.

Measurement
- Completion time: self-reported or automated tracking with timestamps.
- Work process adherence: standardized checklist.
- Environmental factors: work hours, lighting, temperature, equipment availability.
- Human factors: employee experience, skills, stress levels.

Analysis
- Regression analysis to identify significant factors affecting completion time.
- Chi-squared test for categorical variables and ANOVA for continuous variables.
- Time series analysis to detect temporal patterns.

Decision / stopping rule
- The experiment will run for a predetermined period, and data will be collected from multiple iterations.
- A significance level of α = 0.05 will be used to determine statistical significance.
- We will examine the Evans-Newton diagram to aid in explaining model fit, with a preference for parsimonious models.

Limitations
- Self-reported data may introduce bias.
- External factors not controlled in the RCE could affect outcomes.
- Seasonal or weekly patterns may need special handling in time series analysis.
- Generalizability to all similar sites with identical processes might be limited due to site-specific characteristics.
